subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: Should configured exec deny patterns be a native cross-host policy that overrides broad allow/trust decisions but permits only explicit one-shot human approval, as proposed by the linked implementation candidate?
rationale: This is a durable command-authorization contract: choosing hard denial versus approval-gated execution, durable-trust behavior, and persisted policy ownership cannot be resolved safely by automation.

options.title: Sponsor the approval-gated design
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101276 if its cross-host, upgrade, and persisted-config proof confirms deny-over-allow with one-shot human approval.

options.title: Require hard-deny semantics
options.body: Keep the issue open and direct a narrower revision if deny matches must never be executable, including after human approval.

options.title: Defer native policy expansion
options.body: Keep the issue open without merging the candidate if maintainers do not want to extend the core exec-authorization contract now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the approval-gated design
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101276 if its cross-host, upgrade, and persisted-config proof confirms deny-over-allow with one-shot human approval.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied maintainer discussion already frames the security-policy boundary and the affected implementation surfaces.
